question: What is the main difference between endocrine and exocrine glands?

options.A: Endocrine glands lack ducts and secrete directly into blood
options.B: Endocrine glands have special tubes for drainage
options.C: Exocrine glands rely on reticular fibers

explanation: Endocrine glands do not have ducts, so they release their chemical messengers straight into the surrounding fluid and blood vessels. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why are there so many tiny blood vessels around endocrine cells?

options.A: To give physical support to delicate cells
options.B: To filter out unwanted chemicals before they travel
options.C: To allow rapid movement of hormones directly into the blood
options.D: To keep harmful germs away from hormones

explanation: Having many small, porous blood vessels nearby ensures that hormones quickly enter the bloodstream to reach their target organs. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h1)

question: Where is the pituitary gland located in the skull?

options.A: Inside the sella turcica of the sphenoid bone
options.B: Attached to the back of the skull

explanation: The pituitary gland rests securely inside a small, bony depression called the sella turcica. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main job of the hypophyseal portal system?

options.A: Carrying hormones to the rest of the body
options.C: Draining extra fluid away from the brain
options.D: Transporting hypothalamic signals to the anterior pituitary

explanation: Portal veins carry chemical signals directly from the hypothalamus to the front part of the pituitary gland without mixing into general circulation first. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the gel-like fluid inside thyroid follicles called?
explanation: Thyroid follicles store their hormone materials inside a thick, protein-rich fluid known as colloid. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which cells in the parathyroid glands make parathyroid hormone?
explanation: Chief cells are the primary cells responsible for making parathyroid hormone in the parathyroid glands. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which middle zone of the adrenal cortex produces cortisol?
explanation: The zona fasciculata is the wide middle layer of the adrenal cortex that makes cortisol. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h4)

question: What type of cells make up the inner adrenal medulla?
explanation: Chromaffin cells are specialized cells that release adrenaline and noradrenaline directly into nearby blood sinuses. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which cells in the pancreas produce insulin?
explanation: Beta cells are located in the center of the pancreatic islets and produce insulin to lower blood sugar. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main job of alpha cells in the pancreas?

options.D: Releasing glucagon to raise blood sugar

explanation: Alpha cells release glucagon when blood sugar is low, telling the liver to release stored glucose. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h5)

question: What hormone is produced by the pineal gland?
explanation: Pineal cells produce melatonin, which helps regulate sleep-wake cycles and your internal body clock. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h6)

question: Where is the thymus gland located during its active development?
explanation: The thymus sits in the upper chest area, just behind the sternum, during its active developmental phases. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which hormone is produced by the kidneys?
explanation: The kidneys release erythropoietin to signal the bone marrow to make more red blood cells when oxygen levels are low. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main role of enteroendocrine cells in the gut?
explanation: Enteroendocrine cells release local hormones that control gut movement, digestive juices, and acid production. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h7)

question: What type of tiny blood vessels are usually found inside endocrine glands?
explanation: Fenestrated capillaries have tiny pores that let newly made hormones easily pass into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h8)

question: Which feature is NOT found in standard endocrine glands?

options.C: Cells arranged in cords or clumps

explanation: Endocrine glands do not have ducts; they are ductless organs that release their products straight into the blood. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h8)
